memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When you march up to attack a city, make its people an offer of peace. If they accept and open their gates, all the people in it shall be subject to forced labor and shall work for you. If they refuse to make peace and they engage you in battle, lay siege to that city. - Deut 20:10-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before attacking a distant city, Israel was first to offer terms of peace. War was not to be the immediate resort. God required that an offer of peace be extended first, giving the city an opportunity to avoid bloodshed altogether. Only if peace was refused was the battle to proceed.

This reveals that even in the context of warfare, God's preference was for peace where possible. He is not bloodthirsty. The offer of peace came first. This restraint set Israel apart from the ruthless conquerors of the ancient world, who often destroyed without warning or mercy.

While these were specific military instructions for Israel's situation, they reflect God's enduring character as a God who seeks peace. And how gloriously this points to the gospel. God, against whom we had rebelled, took the initiative to offer us peace. He did not wait for us to come to Him; He came to us in Christ, offering reconciliation while we were still His enemies (Rom 5:8-10). The gospel is God's offer of peace extended to a rebellious world. And He calls us, too, to be peacemakers, to seek peace with others wherever we can (Rom 12:18). Have you received the peace God offers you in Christ, and are you extending that peace-seeking spirit to those around you?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you received the peace God offers in Christ?
2. Where are you tempted to fight when you could seek peace?
3. How can you be a peacemaker this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for taking the first step to offer me peace in Christ. Make me a peacemaker who seeks reconciliation wherever I can. Amen.
